text.p: Middle-order batsman Ijaz Ahmed led Pakistan's resistance as they toiled to 197 all out against West Indies in their World Series match at the Gabba on Friday.
Sent into bat by West Indies captain Courtney Walsh, Pakistan stumbled to 47 for four before Ijaz rallied the innings with the help of wicketkeeper Moin Khan.
Ijaz played a responsible role to weather the early crisis, gradually shedding his cautious approach to score 59 in almost three hours at the crease.
Moin lifted the total with a late flurry to score 43 in 52 balls, including one towering straight six, before the Pakistan innings ended with one ball left of their 50 overs.
Walsh justified his decision after winning the toss when he exploited the early bounce in the pitch to remove openers Aamir Sohail and Shahid Afridi cheaply with successive balls.
The veteran fast bowler returned late in the innings to dismiss Ijaz when he attempted a late cut only to edge a simple catch to wicketkeeper Junior Murray.
Ijaz enjoyed a reprieve with his score on 31 when fast bowler Nixon McLean dropped a straightforward catch on the fine leg boundary.
Batting at number five, Ijaz was forced to rely heavily on singles to build his score although indecisive running between the wickets caused problems for his batting partners.
Fast bowler Ian Bishop was the pick of West Indies' bowlers with figures of four for 38 in 9.5 overs.
Pakistan and Australia lead the triangular competition with four points, two points clear of West Indies. Hosts Australia have played four games, one more than their rivals.
